thresholdNote: Candidate = robust change in HH browse intensity between the pair dates under an ensemble of 12 settings (thresholds 0.16/0.22/0.30 normalised, median windows 3/5, MMU 20/60 px). Agreement across settings is a robustness measure, not a probability.

candidates.title: Far east bank
candidates.question: This ground went dark as the river rose in July, then came back bright and stayed bright. What is there now — crop, sand, or the edge of a settlement?

crosscheck.reading: Optical saw open water on 13% of this core on 4 Jul and almost none (0.5%) on 12 Oct; C-band called it land on both of its dates. Two independent sensors agree with the NISAR story: real July water, gone by October.

candidates.title: North-west channel char
candidates.question: Open water here in June and July; by October it is the brightest ground in the whole case. New sandbar, or land that dried and cracked?

crosscheck.reading: Optical saw no open water here on either clear date, and C-band agrees the ground emerged by October. So the July NISAR darkness was a smooth wet surface — flooded mud or wet sand — not a lake. The question below is the one a person on the ground can settle.

candidates.title: North-east low ground
candidates.question: Everything around it dried as the river fell — this patch went the other way and got darker. Standing water left behind, or low wet land?

crosscheck.reading: Optical water coverage grew from 28% to 43% between 4 Jul and 12 Oct, and C-band calls this ground water-like on both dates. The NISAR darkening is real: standing water expanded here while the river around it fell.
